solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ward's disadvantage?

parts.note: the word ward is draw spelt backwards, so a phrase meaning '...' describes how to make it

explanation.surface: A question about what handicap a ward of court might suffer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: take DRAW and write it back, and you get WARD. The question mark flags that the wordplay works in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawback is a snag or downside, a straightforward synonym for a disadvantage.

clue.text: Tot runs into mother's embrace

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside another
the mother's embrace wraps around the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: a dam is a mother animal, especially of livestock
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A toddler dashes into a parent's open arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a small child, but here it is a small measure of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a small serving of spirits, and a dram is the Scottish word for the same small measure of whisky.

clue.text: Expert turning up in hotel bar

indicators.note: turning up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A specialist shows up at the bar of a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turning up' means read from bottom to top: ELBA, spanning 'hotEL BAr', read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An able person is skilled or competent, so the adjective expert is a close synonym.

clue.text: Film making you fed up

definitions.meaning: A 1996 British film about a colliery brass band
British slang for annoyed or thoroughly disgruntled

explanation.surface: A film that leaves its audience bored and grumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: Brassed off is British slang; the film of that name is set in a Yorkshire mining town whose pit is closing.
explanation.definitionFit: The film title is the answer itself, and as slang the phrase means annoyed or disgruntled.

clue.text: Nuts for a bird

definitions.meaning: nuts is slang for crazy or mad
a well-known bird which lays its eggs in other birds' nests

explanation.surface: Nuts put out to feed a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuckoo is informal for crazy, and it is also the name of a familiar migratory bird.

clue.text: Love piano accompaniment for American piece of music

indicators.note: accompaniment for says the first pieces go along with the last, side by side

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A romantic piano accompaniment written for an American musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus is the Latin word used for a numbered musical work or composition.

clue.text: Writer with song preference

parts.note: a pen is the thing you write with
a chant is a simple repetitive song

explanation.surface: A songwriter states what they like best.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a strong liking or inclination for something, so it means a preference.

clue.text: Superficial sort implicated in leak

indicators.note: implicated in says one piece is caught up inside the other

parts.note: to seep is to leak out slowly
kind means sort or type

explanation.surface: A shallow kind of person is found to be involved in leaking secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort' and 'leak' read as a person and a press scandal; they are KIND and SEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something skin-deep goes no further than the surface, the idiom for being shallow.

clue.text: Everyone in church will welcome a marriage

indicators.note: will welcome says the outer letters take in the next piece

parts.note: all in means everyone included
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: All the congregation will welcome a wedding in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Everyone in' looks like a container instruction, but it is the phrase ALL IN; the A then goes between its I and N.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a union or bond, and a marriage is a union of two people or families.

clue.text: One who's against settling in Chiantishire

indicators.note: settling in says the letters sit inside the longer word

explanation.surface: An opponent of incomers settling in Tuscany.
explanation.walkthrough: Chiantishire is a jokey name for Tuscany, home of Chianti wine, where many British people own holiday homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti as a noun is a person opposed to something, an informal word for an opponent.

clue.text: Met the girl repairing camera accessory

indicators.note: repairing means putting these letters back together in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone encountered a young woman fixing a part for a camera.
explanation.definitionFit: A light meter measures brightness so a photographer can set exposure, an accessory for a camera.

clue.text: Very surprised when hedonist collapses

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'

indicators.note: collapses means the letters fall apart and are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Onlookers are shocked when a pleasure-seeker falls over.
explanation.definitionFit: Astonished is a synonym of amazed, being greatly surprised.

clue.text: Mischievous, like Conservative infiltrating political meeting

indicators.note: infiltrating says these pieces get inside the other one

parts.note: a rally is a mass political meeting
as means like

explanation.surface: A cheeky Tory sneaks into an opponents' political meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Rascally describes behaviour like a rascal, a scamp or rogue, so it means naughty or mischievous.

clue.text: Rational article about family

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: an article is an object, a thing
kin means family or relatives

explanation.surface: A sensible piece of writing about family life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a grammatical article or a newspaper piece, but here it means an object.
explanation.definitionFit: A thinking person is one who reasons, so as an adjective it means rational or intelligent.

clue.text: Garden pests concealed in sap, unusually

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other
unusually says the letters of sap appear in an unusual order

parts.note: hid means concealed

explanation.surface: Insects lurk hidden in plant sap, which is odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges the clue word sap to APS, which holds the synonym for 'concealed'; the surface hides the pests in the plant's own juice.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphids are greenfly and blackfly, tiny sap-sucking insects that plague gardeners.

clue.text: Transfer some cash

definitions.meaning: to switch from one train or bus to another

explanation.surface: Moving a small amount of money between accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: To change is to switch trains or buses, and loose coins are called change.

clue.text: Phone crowd of people — namely about fifty

parts.note: a mob is a large unruly crowd

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes round the next

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, meaning namely
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Phoning a crowd of roughly fifty people.
explanation.definitionFit: Mobile is the British name for a cellphone, a portable telephone.

clue.text: Container for angler's bait is a problem

definitions.meaning: a tin holding worms used as bait for fishing
an idiom for a complicated situation that causes trouble once opened up

explanation.surface: A fishing bait tin turns out to be troublesome.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a tin holding worms; figuratively the idiom for a tangled matter best left alone.

clue.text: Food shop cut delivery by 50%

indicators.note: cut says the word is shortened
by 50% says only the first half of the word is kept

explanation.surface: A grocer halves its deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling cooked meats, cheeses and prepared food.

clue.text: One's quiet before end of birthday party game

indicators.note: before says the first pieces come ahead of the last

parts.note: I is one, so one's is I'S
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

indicators.note: end of says only the final letter of birthday is used

explanation.surface: Someone goes quiet near the close of a birthday party game.
explanation.definitionFit: I-spy is a guessing game for children where players find things beginning with a given letter.

clue.text: Next to odd slices of onion, large cut of meat

indicators.note: next to says the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: odd slices of says to take the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A big joint of meat served beside sliced onion.
explanation.definitionFit: Loin is a prime cut of meat from either side of an animal's backbone.

clue.text: Teacher, one with tension after end of term

indicators.note: end of says only the final letter of term is used

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
stress means tension or strain

explanation.surface: A teacher under strain once the school term finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the term's last letter ahead of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistress is an old-fashioned word for a female schoolteacher, as in history mistress.

clue.text: Goya organised course of exercises

indicators.note: organised says the letters are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: The painter Goya set up a fitness class.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoga is a discipline of postures and breathing practised as a regime of exercise.

clue.text: Out of control, they rail with gusto

indicators.note: out of control says the letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Angry people rant furiously, carried away by passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartily means wholeheartedly and enthusiastically, doing something with zest.
